root_cause.text: The `rt2x00usb` driver incorrectly associates the lifetime of the device-managed USB anchor resource with the parent USB device (`usb_dev->dev`) instead of the USB interface (`usb_intf->dev`), leading to memory leaks when the driver is unbound without physical disconnection.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the allocation of `rt2x00dev->anchor` is changed from `devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev, ...)`. The commit message explains that "USB drivers bind to USB interfaces and any device managed resources should have their lifetime tied to the interface rather than parent USB device" to avoid memory leaks on driver unbind.

bic_trace_step.reason: In rt2x00usb_probe, the code allocates the USB anchor using devm_kmalloc with '&usb_dev->dev' (the parent USB device) instead of '&usb_intf->dev' (the USB interface): 'rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, sizeof(struct usb_anchor), GFP_KERNEL);'.
